Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play · Nature & food

hunt verb and noun

animals

also hunting, go hunting, hunter, the hunt, huntsman, hunting dog, hunting gear

classical

Cic. Fam. 2.11.2: quī vēnārī solent (Lewis & Short)
Verg. G. 3.410: canibus leporem
Traupman 48
Traupman 330

vēnor, vēnārī, vēnātus sum

verb, first conjugation, deponent: alone, or with the accusative of the game

Also, figuratively, to hunt after something (votes: Hor. Ep. 1.19.37). Vēnātum īre, to go hunting (Verg. A. 4.117).

Other words

  • vēnātiō, vēnātiōnis f. — hunting, a hunt

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 4.1: multum sunt in vēnātiōnibus (Lewis & Short); Cic. Sen. 56; Traupman 48

    Also a beast-hunt staged in the arena (Cic. Off. 2.55) and the game that is caught (Liv. 35.49.6).

  • vēnātor, vēnātōris m. — a hunter

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 2.40 (Lewis & Short); Hor. C. 1.1.25

    Feminine vēnātrīx. A hunting dog is canis vēnāticus (Plaut.; Traupman 330).

  • vēnātus, vēnātūs m. — hunting, the hunt

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Traupman 330

Examples

  • vēnor aliquandō, sed nōn sine pugillāribus, ut quamvīs nihil cēperim nōn nihil referam

    I hunt sometimes, but not without my notebooks, so that even if I catch nothing I bring something backPlin. Ep. 9.36.6

  • Illīcne umquam vēnāris? — Etiam. Vēnor cunīculōs, phāsiānās, cervōs.

    Do you ever hunt there? — Yes. I hunt rabbits, pheasants and deer.Traupman 140

  • canis vēnāticus

    a hunting dogTraupman 48; Cic. Verr. 2.4.31 (Lewis & Short s.v. vēnāticus)

  • īnstrūmentum vēnātōrium

    hunting gearTraupman 48

See also chase, fishing, gun, look for, capture.
